The `Relation#create` examples show the result of `users.create(name: 'fxn')` attached to an extra argument-less `users.create` call:

title: docs(axum): recommend actor pattern for concurrent WebSocket read/write

pull_request.title: docs(axum): recommend actor pattern for concurrent WebSocket read/write
pull_request.description:
## Motivation

The WebSocket module docs suggest `StreamExt::split` as the way to read and write concurrently. Splitting wraps each half in a lock that must be acquired on every operation, which adds avoidable overhead. Upstream issue tokio-rs/axum#3793 proposes highlighting the actor pattern as the higher-performance alternative, and tokio-rs/axum#3786 already laid the groundwork by documenting that `WebSocket::recv` is cancel safe.

## Solution

Rework the "Read and write concurrently" section in `axum/src/extract/ws.rs`:

- Lead with the actor pattern: a single task owns the socket and uses `tokio::select!` to race `WebSocket::recv` (cancel safe) against an `mpsc` channel that other tasks use to send messages to the client. Links to [Actors with Tokio](https://ryhl.io/blog/actors-with-tokio/) for background.
- Keep `StreamExt::split` as a documented alternative, with a note about its per-operation locking overhead.

Both examples are compile-checked doc tests. Verified with `cargo test -p axum --all-features --doc ws` and `cargo doc` using CI's rustdoc flags (`-D rustdoc::all -A rustdoc::private-doc-tests`); the test-only hidden line does not appear in the rendered docs.

## Summary

Bumps `body-parser` from `^2.2.1` to `^2.3.0` to remediate **CVE-2026-12590** (GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6).

body-parser `>=2.0.0 <2.3.0` (and `<1.20.6` on the 1.x line) fails open when

title: fix(axum-extra): handle missing optional typed headers

pull_request.title: fix(axum-extra): handle missing optional typed headers
pull_request.description:
## Motivation

`Option<TypedHeader<T>>` currently decodes the header values before checking whether the header exists.

Some `headers::Header` implementations successfully decode an empty iterator. For example, `headers::Cookie` decodes an empty iterator into an empty cookie collection. As a result, `Option<TypedHeader<headers::Cookie>>` returns `Some(empty Cookie)` when the `Cookie` header is completely absent.

This contradicts the documented behavior of optional extractors, where a missing header should return `None`.

## Solution

Check whether the header exists before decoding its values.

If the header is absent, return `None` immediately. If it is present, preserve the existing decoding behavior and return `TypedHeaderRejection` when parsing fails.

title: fix(axum-extra): reject opaque Attachment filenames

pull_request.title: fix(axum-extra): reject opaque Attachment filenames
pull_request.description:
## Motivation

`Attachment::filename` accepts any value that converts to `HeaderValue`. This includes values containing opaque bytes, which are valid header values but cannot be represented by `HeaderValue::to_str`.

`Attachment::into_response` currently calls `to_str().expect(...)` on the stored filename. Passing an opaque `HeaderValue` therefore causes response construction to panic.

## Solution

Validate that the converted `HeaderValue` has a string representation before storing it. If it does not, use the existing invalid-filename behavior: log an error and omit the filename from `Content-Disposition`.

Add a regression test using a filename containing `0xff` and verify the response falls back to `Content-Disposition: attachment`.

Verified with `cargo test -p axum-extra --lib --no-default-features --features attachment response::attachment::tests`.

title: fix(res.send): preserve ETag generation with Transfer-Encoding

pull_request.title: fix(res.send): preserve ETag generation with Transfer-Encoding
pull_request.description:
Preserve automatic ETag generation when `res.send()` is used with a pre-existing `Transfer-Encoding` header.


Commit `18e5985b` correctly prevented `Content-Length` from being added when `Transfer-Encoding` is present, but it also moved the body-length calculation inside the same condition.

Because automatic ETag generation depends on the calculated body length, responses using `Transfer-Encoding` stopped receiving an ETag.

pull_request.title: fix: reset skipped-nodes stack on getValue entry to prevent slice overflow panic [#4818]
pull_request.description:
Fixes #4818

## Root cause

With `HandleMethodNotAllowed = true`, `handleHTTPRequest` calls `getValue`
once per method tree in the `HandleMethodNotAllowed` loop, reusing the
same `c.skippedNodes` stack from the pooled Context. `getValue` pushes
entries onto the stack via a raw reslice (`[:index+1]`) that cannot grow
past `engine.maxSections`. Without resetting the stack on entry, residue
from a previous tree accumulates until the next reslice exceeds capacity
and panics with "slice bounds out of range".

## Fix

Reset `*skippedNodes = (*skippedNodes)[:0]` at the top of `getValue` so
every call starts with an empty stack. This is the single point that
covers all callers, including the `HandleMethodNotAllowed` loop.

## Tests

- `TestIssue4818_skippedNodesOverflow_Panic`: original repro from the
  issue — POST to a route that causes skippedNodes residue to exceed
  `maxSections` capacity. Confirms no panic and 404 (correct).
- `TestIssue4818_MethodNotAllowedStillWorks`: PATCH a path that only
  has a GET route, confirming the `HandleMethodNotAllowed` loop still
  produces a correct 405 with Allow header.
- `TestIssue4818_MethodNotAllowedManyTrees`: stress test with 9 method
  trees targeting a single GET-only path, verifying no overflow.

pull_request.title: fix: only treat whole `node_modules` path segments as dependencies (fix #17467)
pull_request.description:
Fixes #17467.

`isInNodeModules` decides whether a module belongs to the user or to a dependency, and it does that with `id.includes('node_modules')`. A project whose directory name merely *contains* that string — `node_modules_bug`, `my_node_modules`, a checkout named after this very issue — has every one of its own files classified as a dependency.

The symptom in the original report (a hard `Failed to parse source for import analysis` on inline `<script type="module">`) is gone: `htmlProxyRE` now accepts `html-proxy` anywhere in the query, so the extra `?v=` no longer breaks the match. The cause is still there, and it still misbehaves, just more quietly. Building `main` and pointing two otherwise identical projects at it:

```
root                : node_modules_bug
inline-script id    : <root>/index.html?v=40b7386f&html-proxy&index=0.js
/src/main.js id     : <root>/src/main.js?v=40b7386f
sourcemapIgnoreList : true
x_google_ignoreList : [0]

root                : plain_project
inline-script id    : <root>/index.html?html-proxy&index=0.js
/src/main.js id     : <root>/src/main.js
sourcemapIgnoreList : false
x_google_ignoreList : undefined
```

Two things there. `ensureVersionQuery` stamps the optimizer's `browserHash` onto every one of the project's own modules, so they get invalidated whenever deps are re-optimized. And because `server.sourcemapIgnoreList` defaults to `isInNodeModules`, Vite emits `x_google_ignoreList` for the user's own source — DevTools hides your application code from stack traces and won't step into it. Same substring reaches `external.ts` (a linked workspace package under such a root gets externalized for SSR), `optimizer/scan.ts`, `preAlias.ts` and `resolve.ts`.

## The change

`node_modules` now has to be a whole path segment:

```js
const inNodeModulesRE = /(?:^|[\\/])node_modules(?:[\\/]|$)/
```

Both separator classes are needed — most call sites hand over a normalized posix id, but `packages.ts` and `tryFsResolve` pass native paths, so on Windows they arrive with backslashes. The trailing `|$` keeps the old answer for a path that *is* a `node_modules` directory with nothing after it; nothing in the tree depends on that today, but making the segment boundary the only difference from `main` keeps the change to exactly the reported bug.

This is the minimum the reporter asked for, not the "complete fix" also described in the issue. Making `isInNodeModules` aware of `config.root` (so a project that genuinely lives *inside* `node_modules` is treated as first-party) needs a root threaded through thirteen call sites, several of which run before the config is resolved, and it changes behaviour for the much more common linked-package case. It seems like a separate discussion, and I'd rather not smuggle it in here. Happy to open a follow-up if you want it.

## Prior attempts

#21549 (closed by its author) and #21638 (auto-closed as bot-likely) both went at the leading separator only. Neither got review comments, so I don't think there is a rejected design here, but flagging them so this isn't reviewed as a duplicate.

## Test

Unit tests on `isInNodeModules` itself. The negative cases are the point — they're what tells a correct fix from a half one. I checked that by breaking it three ways and re-running:

- back to `includes('node_modules')` → fails on `/project/node_modules_bug/src/main.js`
- leading separator only, `/(?:^|[\\/])node_modules/` → fails on the same case
- trailing separator only, `/node_modules(?:[\\/]|$)/` → fails on `/project/my_node_modules/src/main.js`

No playground test: reproducing this needs a project directory named `node_modules_bug`, and adding one to `playground/` would collide with the repo's own `**/node_modules/**` ignores in the watcher, the workspace globs and the test runner. If you'd rather see it covered end-to-end I can add a fixture that builds the path at runtime instead.

title: feat(router): add QUERY method shortcut for RFC 10008

pull_request.title: feat(router): add QUERY method shortcut for RFC 10008
pull_request.description:
## Description

Add a `QUERY()` router method as a shortcut for `Handle("QUERY", path, handlers)`, following the same pattern as `GET`, `POST`, `HEAD`, and other HTTP method shortcuts.

The `QUERY` method is defined by [RFC 10008](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc10008/) and allows sending a query in the request body, similar to `GET` but with a body. This is useful for complex queries that exceed URL length limits or need structured request bodies.

Go's `net/http` does not yet expose an `http.MethodQuery` constant (tracked in [golang/go#80058](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/80058)), so the literal string `"QUERY"` is used. Gin already routes based on `Request.Method`, and Go does not restrict HTTP methods to a predefined set, so this works without waiting for standard library support.

## Changes

- `routergroup.go`: Add `QUERY()` method on `*RouterGroup`
- `gin_test.go`: Add `TestRouterQueryMethod` test verifying routing and that other methods don't match

## Usage

```go
router := gin.Default()
router.QUERY("/search", func(c *gin.Context) {
    // Query body is in c.Request.Body
    c.JSON(200, gin.H{"result": "ok"})
})
```

Closes #4721

Added a new `(*gin.Context).Scheme()` helper method that reliably returns the protocol scheme ("http" or "https") of the request, with **reverse proxy support**.

title: pki: honor skip_install_trust for explicit tls internal issuers

pull_request.title: pki: honor skip_install_trust for explicit tls internal issuers
pull_request.description:
Site-level `tls internal` creates its own CA independently of `auto_https`. Since `buildPKIApp()` only pre-registered a CA with `install_trust: false` when `auto_https` wasn't fully disabled, that CA was instead created later at runtime with trust installation left on whenever `auto_https` was off, silently ignoring `skip_install_trust`.

This adds a check that looks at each site's configured internal issuer (matched by type, so it covers both the shorthand and the explicit `ca <id>` form) and registers its CA with `install_trust: false`, regardless of `auto_https`.

Added tests for: the default `local` CA case, a custom-named CA via the explicit issuer form, and a no-regression check that no `pki` app is emitted when no site uses an internal issuer.

Fixes #7893

Traced the root cause and verified the fix, used Claude to help draft parts of the code and tests, reviewed each line before submitting.

### Motivation / Background

This came up in https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/discussions/2186 and was addressed in https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/pull/2291. This PR is the upstreamed version of that. 

In local installations that don't use HTTPS and where the app is accessed within a local network, requests won't be performed from [a secure context](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Defenses/Secure_Contexts#potentially_trustworthy_origins). In this case, the browser won't send the `Sec-Fetch-Site` header. This means non-GET requests will be rejected because CSRF protection will fail when using the header-only approach.

### Detail

With this change, we allow these requests with missing `Sec-Fetch-Site` headers if:

- They happen over HTTP
- The app is not configured to force SSL

The `Origin` check always happens in any case.

title: fix(framework): mark migration scripts as completed only after successful run

pull_request.title: fix(framework): mark migration scripts as completed only after successful run
pull_request.description:
Previously, a migration script was marked as completed before it actually ran, then deleted on failure to denote that it needs to run again. However, in situations where the process is killed or a database deadlock happens  that crashes the command, the migration script is left as completed, so re-running migrations doesn't run it again.

This PR fixes the issue by changing how a migration script is considered as completed. We use the `finished_at` property, and it's set only after the migration script actually complete. So, if the migration script fails or application crashes, the migration script re-executes.

The PR also handles running migrations concurrently, making sure only one process runs a migration script at a time.

Logged message when re-running migrations with a migration script that wasn't completed:

```bash
info:    Running migration scripts...
warn:    Migration script /Users/shahednasser/test-projects/medusa-resolutions/src/migration-scripts/sleep-migration-script.ts did not complete during a previous run and is being executed again
info:    Running migration script /Users/shahednasser/test-projects/medusa-resolutions/src/migration-scripts/sleep-migration-script.ts
```

Closes DX-2878

title: Narrow scope of Docker build cache in Github workflows

pull_request.title: Narrow scope of Docker build cache in Github workflows
pull_request.description:
The `build-container-image.yml` workflow runs the image builds for linux/amd64, linux/arm64 and is invoked twice in parallel — once for `Dockerfile`, once for `streaming/Dockerfile`. That's four jobs writing to the GitHub Actions cache simultaneously. This workflow cache configuration is then inherited by other build jobs which do not explicitly disable caching (nightly and release builds) across every commit.

Per https://docs.docker.com/build/cache/backends/gha/

> Scope is a key used to identify the cache object. By default, it is set to buildkit. If you build multiple images, each build will overwrite the cache of the previous, leaving only the final cache.
> 
> To preserve the cache for multiple builds, you can specify this scope attribute with a specific name. In the following example, the cache is set to the image name, to ensure each image gets its own cache

This PR adds `scope=` to the `cache-from` and `cache-to` parameters in `build-container-image.yml`, keyed on the Dockerfile content hash and the target platform.

The 10GB overall limit of the `gha` cache still applies.

title: Add workflow to manually trigger Docker & Publish

pull_request.title: Add workflow to manually trigger Docker & Publish
pull_request.description:
Existing workflow with releases does:

job1: create tag & release → job2: publish docker image → job3: trigger saleor cloud release

[recently](https://github.com/saleor/saleor/actions/runs/24142808770/job/70448622528#step:5:11) it failed (github server error) in release step, we ended up locked:
1. Tag created (and we have immutable tags)
2. Docker not built
3. We can't build Docker, because it requires job1 to finish...
4. ... we can't re-run job1, because tag exists

To solve this issue and continue release we need to unlock ourselves, there are 2 easy ways
1. Gracefully ignore tag creation failure and continue
2. Manually dispatch workflow with tag prepared

We agreed with @magul option 2 is better. It will result with the same effect, but has some extra power to manually dispatch some non-standard version if needed

This PR adds new workflow that copies job2 and job3 from existing workflow, but version string is passed from manual workflow dispatch

title: Refactor `CommandRecorder` to store args and kwargs separately

pull_request.title: Refactor `CommandRecorder` to store args and kwargs separately
pull_request.description:
`recorder.commands` now stores each recorded migration command as `[cmd, args, kwargs, block]` (4-element) instead of `[cmd, args, block]` (3-element) with kwargs bundled into a trailing hash inside `args`. Code that inspects `recorder.commands` directly needs to adapt to the new tuple shape.

The old encoding was inherited from the `ruby2_keywords` transition period, where kwargs and positional args had to travel through a single flat array with the trailing hash marked as kwargs. Since Rails now requires Ruby 3.3.1+ (where kwargs are properly separated), the shim is no longer needed. All `invert_*` helpers now receive args and kwargs separately — removing the `.extract_options!`, `.last.is_a?(Hash)`, and `args << options` patterns that the `ruby2_keywords` idiom required.

This direction is aligned with a Ruby proposal to deprecate `ruby2_keywords` in the future (https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/22205), since libraries that only support Ruby 3.0+ no longer need it.

+change on `Order.transactions`.
+
+Opening `Order.transactions` would publish the whole type — `externalUrl` (PSP back-office deep
+link), `events` (internal ledger, staff identities, idempotency keys), `createdBy`, `name`,
+`message` — and its `id`, which is the transaction `token`, a capability accepted by the
+unauthenticated `transactionInitialize`/`transactionProcess` mutations. Allowlisting fields on the
+existing type is not an option either: `PermissionsField` raises, and `[TransactionItem!]!` with
+non-null fields means one denied field nulls the entire order. The projection is an allowlist, so
+fields added to `TransactionItem` later cannot leak through it.
+
+The field is meant to be queried by a storefront (account page, order summary) to show the money
+that moved to and from the customer. That is why transactions with all amounts at zero are
+filtered out: they are abandoned payment attempts and carry no information for the customer.
+
+Card data is stripped for the same reason. `paymentMethodDetails` reuses the shared
+`PaymentMethodDetails` types, but the resolver blanks `firstDigits`, `lastDigits`, `expMonth` and
+`expYear` on a copy of the transaction, so a public caller sees the payment method and the brand
+and nothing that identifies the instrument. Staff read the full card data through
+`Order.transactions` as before.

title: fix(payment-stripe): handle Stripe webhook signature errors

pull_request.description:
## Summary

**What** — What changes are introduced in this PR?

`StripeBase.constructWebhookEvent` calls `this.stripe_.webhooks.constructEvent(...)` and returns its result without a `try/catch`. This PR wraps that call in a `try/catch` that rethrows through the existing `buildError` helper, so a failure during webhook construction produces the same normalized error as every other method in the provider. No behavior changes on the happy path.

**Why** — Why are these changes relevant or necessary?

Stripe's `constructEvent` throws a `StripeSignatureVerificationError` when the payload signature can't be verified (an invalid or spoofed `stripe-signature` header, or a missing/misconfigured `webhookSecret`). `constructWebhookEvent` is the only method in `stripe-base.ts` that lets a Stripe SDK error escape unwrapped. Every other method (`cancelPayment`, `capturePayment`, `refundPayment`, `retrievePayment`, `updatePayment`, the account-holder and payment-method methods, and so on) already wraps its Stripe call in `try/catch` and rethrows via `this.buildError(...)`, producing a consistent `"An error occurred in <method>: <detail>"` message.

Because `getWebhookActionAndData` (which calls `constructWebhookEvent`) runs in the payment webhook subscriber, a verification failure currently surfaces as a raw Stripe error in the webhook processing/retry path, inconsistent with how the rest of the module reports Stripe failures. Wrapping it keeps the error shape uniform and easier to identify in logs.

**How** — How have these changes been implemented?

```diff
   constructWebhookEvent(data: ProviderWebhookPayload["payload"]): Stripe.Event {
     const signature = data.headers["stripe-signature"] as string

-    return this.stripe_.webhooks.constructEvent(
-      data.rawData as string | Buffer,
-      signature,
-      this.options_.webhookSecret
-    )
+    try {
+      return this.stripe_.webhooks.constructEvent(
+        data.rawData as string | Buffer,
+        signature,
+        this.options_.webhookSecret
+      )
+    } catch (error) {
+      throw this.buildError("An error occurred in constructWebhookEvent", error)
+    }
   }
```

The catch block mirrors the surrounding convention exactly: same catch-variable name, same terse message format, and the same untyped-`error` handoff to `buildError` that the other methods use.

Added a unit test to `packages/modules/providers/payment-stripe/src/core/__tests__/stripe-base.spec.ts` that calls `constructWebhookEvent` with an invalid `stripe-signature` header and asserts the thrown error is the normalized `"An error occurred in constructWebhookEvent"` message rather than the raw Stripe error. `constructEvent` performs signature verification locally (no network), so the test is deterministic.

})
// Before: throws Stripe's raw StripeSignatureVerificationError

pull_request.title: Reset `lock_version` after transaction rollback
pull_request.description:
### Motivation / Background

When a record with optimistic locking is successfully saved inside a transaction that later rolls back, the in-memory `lock_version` is left at the incremented value while the database row is reverted to its previous one.
Saving the same instance again then raises `ActiveRecord::StaleObjectError` because the WHERE clause uses the incremented value that no longer exists in the database.

```ruby

Widget.transaction do

title: Acquire reaper_lock in preconnect to avoid racing with the reaper

pull_request.title: Acquire reaper_lock in preconnect to avoid racing with the reaper
pull_request.description:
### Motivation / Background

`test_preconnect` intermittently fails on CI, e.g., [rails-nightly build #4330](https://buildkite.com/rails/rails-nightly/builds/4330#019e6616-bb7b-43f3-be2d-465dbf507100/L11173):

```ruby
ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::ConnectionPoolThreadTest#test_preconnect
Expected #<ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::Mysql2Adapter:0x00000000118c40
  env_name="arunit" role=:writing> to be connected?.
```

The reaper thread calls `preconnect` as part of its maintenance cycle while holding `reaper_lock`. When the test also calls `pool.preconnect` concurrently, the reaper may have a connection checked out via `checkout_for_maintenance`, leaving it in a transient state (`allow_preconnect=false`, `@raw_connection=nil`) that the test's `preconnect` cannot process.

### Detail

This Pull Request wraps `preconnect` in `reaper_lock`, following the same pattern used by `disconnect`, `discard!`, and `with_exclusively_acquired_all_connections` in e45d8acc746. Since `reaper_lock` uses a reentrant `Monitor`, the reaper's own call to `preconnect` (already inside `reaper_lock`) passes through without blocking.

### Additional information

Follow-up to e45d8acc746 ("Lock the pool while performing global operations").

Reproduced locally with Docker MariaDB 11.4 (`--cpus=0.02 --memory=128m`) under concurrent load. Without the fix, `test_preconnect` failed at iterations 7, 16, 36, and 65. With the fix, 100+ iterations passed with `reaper_lock` wait triggered 86+ times. Diagnostic logging branch: https://github.com/yahonda/rails/tree/fix-preconnect-reaper-lock-race-debug

### Checklist

* [x] This Pull Request is related to one change. Unrelated changes should be opened in separate PRs.
* [x] Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why.
* [ ] Tests are added or updated if you fix a bug or add a feature.
* [ ] CHANGELOG files are updated for the changed libraries if there is a behavior change or additional feature. Minor bug fixes and documentation changes should not be included.

-          # connection will go back to the pool, and the next consumer will

pull_request.title: admin: Synchronize server assignment/references to avoid data race
pull_request.description:
Resolves #4260.

While stepping through the stack traces in the above issue, I initially thought the existing [config mutex](https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/blob/master/caddy.go#L133-L134) should cover this situation, however, since we reference [`localAdminServer` (and `remoteAdminServer`)](https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/blob/master/admin.go#L349) in a goroutine later on, it's still possible that the reads on those variables are concurrent with writes.

I added a test that when paired with the `-race` flag consistently fails against tag 2.4.3 (9d4ed3a3236df06e54c80c4f6633b66d68ad3673). With these changes, the test consistently passes with the `-race` flag (at least on my machine 😄).

The addition of a mutex here doesn't seem to appreciably impact performance and motivated my decision to go with a `sync.Mutex` over a `sync.RWMutex`:

```
goos: darwin
goarch: amd64
pkg: github.com/caddyserver/caddy/v2
cpu: Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-5257U CPU @ 2.70GHz

Without synchronization: BenchmarkLoad-4   	    6410	    208997 ns/op
                         BenchmarkLoad-4   	    5682	    205783 ns/op
                         BenchmarkLoad-4   	    6840	    201484 ns/op

With a plain ol mutex:   BenchmarkLoad-4   	    6616	    224705 ns/op
                         BenchmarkLoad-4   	    7945	    202252 ns/op
                         BenchmarkLoad-4   	    6192	    203228 ns/op

With a RWMutex:          BenchmarkLoad-4   	    6112	    205772 ns/op
                         BenchmarkLoad-4   	    6844	    221402 ns/op
                         BenchmarkLoad-4   	    6001	    188549 ns/op
```

IIUC, [CI runs test with `-race` enabled](https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/blob/master/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L108), so this new test should also be useful there as well.

- No breaking changes to existing functionality

- `gin_test.go`: Added `TestEngineHandleContextNoRouteWithEngineMiddleware` — tests NoRoute → HandleContext with both engine and group middleware

- `go test -run "TestEngineHandleContextNoRoute" -v -count=1` — both tests pass
